## Natural history notes

A microscopic colonial green alga characterized by spherical to oval colonies typically containing 8, 16, or 32 closely packed, pear-shaped cells embedded within a gelatinous matrix. Pandorina morum occurs in freshwater habitats such as ponds, lakes, ditches, and slow-moving waters, where its flagellated cells allow the entire colony to swim and orient toward light. It is part of the volvocine lineage of green algae and represents an important intermediate level of colonial organization between unicellular forms and more complex colonies such as Volvox. Like other freshwater phytoplankton, it contributes to primary production and provides food for microscopic aquatic consumers.
